title: MyRecon vs DeHashed: OSINT & Breach Workflows Compared
description: Compare MyRecon and DeHashed: search inputs, breach workflows and verification limits. Choose an OSINT tool for authorized research.
h1: MyRecon vs DeHashed: compare breach and footprint workflows
intro: Looking for a DeHashed alternative depends on the investigation requirements: DeHashed is a commercial search engine indexing historical breach data and asset records. MyRecon provides a free browser-based public username search, email breach detection, and digital footprint audit tools. This page compares their workflows, ethics, and data sources objectively.

sections.heading: What DeHashed is designed to do
sections.body: DeHashed is documented as a commercial asset search engine that indexes historical data breach records, leaked credential datasets, and compromised database dumps. It is primarily used by enterprise security analysts, incident responders, and certified investigators to identify corporate exposure and credential compromise.

sections.heading: Where a MyRecon workflow fits
sections.body: MyRecon focuses on zero-install public-source intelligence and consent-based footprint audits. It allows users to search public handles across 500+ live platforms, check email breach exposures via verified incident metadata, analyze DNS/WHOIS records, and perform digital footprint self-audits without requiring subscription fees or software downloads.

sections.heading: Compare evidence rather than raw record counts
sections.body: The two tools operate under different philosophies and data collection models. DeHashed maintains an indexed historical breach repository, while MyRecon queries live public platform endpoints and ethical breach metadata APIs. Always corroborate results from either tool using primary sources and independently verified documentation.

faq.question: Is MyRecon a free alternative to DeHashed?
faq.answer: For public username searches, email exposure checks, and digital footprint auditing, yes. MyRecon offers free guest scans without registration. However, MyRecon does not host raw plaintext password databases or compromised company dumps.

faq.question: How does MyRecon handle breach searches differently from DeHashed?
faq.answer: MyRecon uses privacy-preserving breach metadata and k-anonymity protocols, confirming whether an email or password hash was exposed in a confirmed incident without storing or displaying sensitive plaintext records.

faq.question: Can I search usernames on both platforms?
faq.answer: Yes. DeHashed searches its historical database for usernames found in past leaks, whereas MyRecon queries 500+ live social, developer, and forum platforms directly in real time to see where the handle is currently active.
